what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: An editor's channel from the page to the agent
sections.para: Editing in a chat loses the page, version and phrase. The site has a lane, an inbox and a vault, but no editor's channel. A key makes a browser an editor's; its reads, sign-offs and fixes on newsroom pages go to an editor vault, and a daily pass acts on them and replies. Five audiences get five lanes; keys should become key pairs.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A key, an editor vault, a daily pass
sections.para: Editing in a chat loses context. A lane, an inbox and a cross-device vault exist; an editor's channel does not. A key turns a browser into an editor's without changing the reader's site. An editor vault holds a subset of my account; a daily pass, or a button, runs checks, releases cheap fixes and proposes the rest. Five lanes; key pairs later.

sections.label: The problem with editing in a chat
sections.line: Edits arrive stripped of page and version
sections.para: Today's wording fix started on one device and was described from memory in a chat on another, so the agent had to find the article. Most edits start on a page, at a version, with a phrase selected, and lose all of it. Worse, a piece I read and find fine leaves no trace, so what I have reviewed stays invisible.

sections.label: What already exists
sections.line: The pane, the lane and the inbox exist
sections.para: Readers already have a vault pane syncing reading and notes between devices through a vault the newsroom cannot open; a lane that sends chosen notes with a read key, read by lane.py; and an inbox any browser can append to, sealed to the reader's public key. The lane only goes one way, and nothing reads it unless asked.

sections.label: A key that makes a browser an editor's
sections.line: A key switches a browser into editor mode
sections.para: The plain reader's site stays as it is. An editor key, carried in a link fragment or QR code, joins a browser to an editor vault holding a subset of my account. It syncs chosen kinds as I read, including page tweaks, and a new Signed off note tied to a version that goes stale when the article changes.

sections.label: The daily pass
sections.line: Daily: checks, cheap fixes released, the rest proposed
sections.para: Once a day and on Process now, the pass pulls the vault, records sign-offs, runs the wording, link, width, quote and summary checks, applies and releases what is cheap to undo, proposes changes to claims or titles, and writes a report back. It works under a behaviour policy, and can still be triggered from a chat.

sections.label: Five audiences, five lanes
sections.line: Five audiences, each with a lane and key
sections.para: The plain reader sends nothing; a reader with a vault syncs their own devices; an anonymous checkbox, off by default, appends only page, kind and phrase and cannot read back; a named reader sends chosen notes with a read key; an editor sends everything and gets answers. Extra fields are opt-in.

sections.label: Keys, and then key pairs
sections.line: Shared keys now, key pairs per person later
sections.para: Two-way access is a vault's read and write keys; append-only is a token. Both are shared secrets, fine for one editor but not a desk. Key pairs per person and agent let messages be signed and sealed, and access be granted and revoked per key. The inbox already seals to a public key; signatures and per-key grants are missing.

sections.label: Where this stands
sections.line: Pieces built; the channel is a brief
sections.para: The pane, the lane, the inbox and append lanes are built and used. The editor key, vault, sign-offs, down lane, anonymous checkbox and daily pass are not. The agent that built the pane takes the browser side, and the newsroom's writing agent takes the pass; a brief maps what exists, the order and the tests.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A design, one editor, shared keys
sections.para: Nothing in the editor's channel is built, and only one person has used the pieces. Shared keys show someone had the key, not who. The anonymous lane hides identity in the record, not in traffic. The pass acts alone only on what is cheap to undo. Editor mode sends more than the lane, so it is scoped to newsroom pages.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A voice memo and the site's own design notes
sections.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026, after the wording fix. It builds on this site's notes on the activity vault, the feedback loop, sending from any browser and the vault opened, and on the wording check in admin/build/wording.py, with related articles on page fixes, undo cost, agent policies and ephemeral vaults.
